<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec id="S0033291724002824_sec_a1">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The association between heatwave and heat-related outcomes in people with mental health conditions with and without psychotropics was unclear.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="S0033291724002824_sec_a2" sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      We identified people with severe mental illness (SMI) and depression, respectively, using Japanese claim data of Ibaraki prefecture during 1/1/2014–31/12/2021. We conducted self-controlled case series to estimate the incidence rate ratio (IRR) of heat-related illness, myocardial infarction and delirium, respectively, during 5-day pre-heatwave, heatwave, and 5-day post-heatwave periods
                      <jats:italic>v.</jats:italic>
                      all other periods (baseline) within an individual, stratified by periods prescribed psychotropics and periods not prescribed psychotropics, respectively.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="S0033291724002824_sec_a3" sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>
                      Among people with SMI, heatwave was associated with an increased rate of heat-related illness
                      <jats:italic>v.</jats:italic>
                      baseline, with no evidence of a difference in the IRRs between those prescribed
                      <jats:italic>v.</jats:italic>
                      not prescribed antipsychotics (IRR: 1.48 [95% CI 1.40–1.56]; 1.45 [95% CI 1.35–1.56] respectively,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      interaction: 0.53). Among people with depression, heatwave was similarly associated with heat-related illness, with no evidence of a difference in the IRRs between those prescribed
                      <jats:italic>v.</jats:italic>
                      not prescribed antidepressants (IRR: 1.54 [95% CI 1.46–1.64]; 1.64 [95% CI 1.57–1.71] respectively,
                      <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>
                      interaction: 0.33). Smaller increased rates of heat-related illness were also observed in pre- and post-heatwave periods,
                      <jats:italic>v.</jats:italic>
                      baseline in both cohorts. There was weak evidence of an increased risk of MI and delirium associated with heatwave
                      <jats:italic>v.</jats:italic>
                      baseline.
                    </jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec id="S0033291724002824_sec_a4" sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We showed an increased risk of heat-related illness, myocardial infarction and delirium associated with heatwave in people with mental health conditions regardless of whether being prescribed psychotropics. Risks of heat-related illness, myocardial infarction and delirium associated with heatwave might not be factors to influence decisions about the routine use of psychotropics.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
title: The role of psychotropics on the associations between extreme temperature and heat-related outcomes among people with mental health conditions: population-based study
